text: {"rules":[{"jurisdiction":"CA","level":"state","category":"screening_restrictions","status":"in_force","title":"California FEHA: source-of-income and credit-history limits in rental screening","requirement":"Owners may not discriminate against, or advertise a preference against, applicants because of source of income, which includes federal, state or local public assistance and housing subsidies such as Section 8 vouchers and HUD-VASH vouchers. Where a government rent subsidy applies, a landlord may not use a financial or income standard that is not based on the portion of rent the tenant pays. In that case, a landlord using credit history must also offer the applicant the option of providing lawful, verifiable alternative evidence of ability to pay, such as government benefit payments, pay records or bank statements. If the applicant elects this option, the landlord must give reasonable time to respond and reasonably consider the alternative evidence in lieu of credit history. Income standards must count the aggregate income of persons residing together on the same basis as that of married persons. Landlords may still ask about the level or source of income, verify employment, request landlord references and verify identity.","key_value":"Source of income (incl.
